hints.title: Separate the lobes
hints.body: Mark the zeros of the factored polynomial and test its sign between consecutive zeros. Name the positive geometric area of each lobe.
hints.recap: A signed integral uses the sign of the curve on each interval; geometric area is always nonnegative.
hints.pitfall: A factor written as r minus x has the opposite sign from x minus r.
hints.pause: Create a sign chart and express each given integral using your lobe areas.

recall.reminder: A signed integral uses the sign of the curve on each interval; geometric area is always nonnegative.

hints.title: Use the overlap
hints.body: Compare the intervals covered by your three equations. Subtracting two integrals with a shared interval isolates the part they do not share.
hints.recap: Signed integrals add over adjacent intervals and subtract over shared intervals.
hints.pitfall: A zero signed total can contain positive geometric area on both sides of the axis.
hints.pause: Solve for the three positive lobe areas and add their magnitudes.

recall.reminder: Signed integrals add over adjacent intervals and subtract over shared intervals.

solution:
Let A,B,C be the positive areas on (0,p),(p,q),(q,r). Factoring the function shows signs +,−,+, so the given integrals give A−B+C=0, A−B=−2 and −B+C=−3.

Subtracting the third equation from the first gives A=3; then B=5 and C=2. The total geometric area is 3+5+2=10.

Answer F: 10.
knowledgePattern: Recover unsigned lobe areas from overlapping signed integrals
